title: Novel Methods for Catheter and Guidewire Segmentation in X-ray Fluoroscopy under a Federated Learning Setting
abstract: arXiv:2609.06876v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Endovascular procedures rely on real-time manipulation of thin instruments, catheters and guidewires, under X-ray fluoroscopy guidance, where accurate visual analysis is essential for procedural safety. Learning-based methods are constrained by structural complexity, data scarcity, and privacy regulations precluding centralised training across institutions. This thesis presents a structure-aware federated learning framework for catheter and guidewire analysis, with four contributions evaluated on real-animal and phantom data.   A benchmark dataset, CathAction, is introduced for catheterisation analysis, with over 600,000 annotated frames and 40,000 segmentation masks. A shape-sensitive loss transforms masks into signed distance maps compared in a structural feature space, improving Dice coefficient by up to 2.9 points across five backbones.   This is extended to federated learning with shape-sensitive loss, preserving geometric consist

translated_title: 联邦学习设置下X射线透视中导管与导丝分割的新方法
translated_abstract: 血管内介入手术需要在X射线透视引导下实时操纵细长器械（导管和导丝），准确的视觉分析对手术安全至关重要。基于学习的方法受到结构复杂性、数据稀缺性以及隐私法规的制约，隐私法规导致无法在各机构间进行集中式训练。本论文提出了一种用于导管和导丝分析的结构感知联邦学习框架，包含四项贡献，并在真实动物数据和体模数据上进行了评估。论文引入了一个用于导管介入分析的基准数据集CathAction，包含超过60万帧标注图像和4万个分割掩码。一种形状敏感损失将掩码转换为符号距离图，并在结构特征空间中进行比较，在五种骨干网络上将Dice系数最多提升了2.9个百分点。该方法进一步扩展到采用形状敏感损失的联邦学习，以保持几何一致性（摘要截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个用于X射线透视下导管和导丝分割的结构感知联邦学习框架，包含超过60万标注帧的CathAction基准数据集，以及可将Dice系数提升最多2.9个百分点的形状敏感损失。
en_tdlr: This thesis proposes a structure-aware federated learning framework for catheter and guidewire segmentation in X-ray fluoroscopy, introducing the CathAction benchmark dataset with over 600,000 annotated frames and a shape-sensitive loss that improves the Dice coefficient by up to 2.9 points.
